Maintain particle locality groups nearby particle data without changing entity identity. Start with kernel access and scoped selections. The checked stage compares default row ordering with opt-in growable cluster stores and exact maintained selection.
For a classifier or maintenance contract, use the spatial reference. The existing spatial clustering page remains available.

Group particles by a bounded grid cell when profiling shows a locality-sensitive access pattern. Start with systems and kernels and selections. This stage executes on host; device movement follows experimental device rules, and spatial classification and maintenance still run on host after copy-back. Locality optimization does not supply an exact neighbor query.
data.compare-row-ordering-with-growable-parti:
Registration chooses the placement policy; it does not classify or move rows. The checked driver runs the same setup under each policy.
def run_stage[partitioned: Bool]() raises: """Checks the same identities and values under both placement policies. Parameters: partitioned: Choose growable cluster stores instead of row ordering. Raises: Error: If classification, selection, movement, or checks fail. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]() world.resources.add(Time(1)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.5, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(1.5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) var excluded = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-1, 0), Int32(1)) world.register_spatial_classifier[spatial_filter]( Grid(cell_size=1), partitioned=partitioned ) world.maintain_spatial() assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5) assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](excluded).x, -1) partitioned=False is the default: maintenance sorts eligible rows by ascending numeric key within their component-defined stores. Equal keys become contiguous; tie order is not guaranteed. partitioned=True keeps one growable dense SoA store per (logical archetype, cluster key). Capacity starts at one row and doubles as needed. There is no fixed partition row limit or separate chunk-size setting; key/cell policy controls population. Store traversal is not globally key-sorted, and separate clusters need not have adjacent allocations.
The figure contrasts the two layouts after explicit maintenance.
The same logical archetype supports two placement policies.
Letter labels are identities and colors plus key labels identify clusters. All component columns and entity IDs move together. Row ordering can move unchanged entities to restore contiguous groups. Partition mode moves a changed identity into its destination cluster and repairs a source swap-removal; growing the destination can relocate its existing rows too. Creation and component transitions stage rows until maintenance; ordinary queries and host/device kernels still visit matching staged rows. Same-composition replacement stays in its current physical store until refreshed. Maintenance releases empty cluster/staging row allocations; nonempty stores retain capacity.
data.declare-eligible-classifier-inputs#Decla:
Keep position, velocity, and time separate from placement policy.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 The classifier below reads Position; movement can write it without changing the entity’s component composition. Stable entity handles survive placement changes, while component references and row indices do not.
Define a deterministic SpatialClassifier and a matching read-only accessor.
comptime spatial_filter = Filter().read[Position]().exclude[Int32]() @fieldwise_init struct Grid(SpatialClassifier): """Classifies eligible particles by a bounded planar Morton cell.""" comptime Accessor = EntityAccessor[spatial_filter] var cell_size: Float64 def classify(self, entity: Self.Accessor) raises -> UInt64: """Reads only the declared position input. Args: entity: Borrowed classifier inputs; never retained. Raises: Error: If the cell width, coordinates, or cell bounds are invalid. Returns: The exact cell's Morton key. """ ref position = entity.get[Position]() return morton_key_3d( grid_cell(Float64(position.x), self.cell_size), grid_cell(Float64(position.y), self.cell_size), ) spatial_filter classifies entities with Position and no Int32 marker. Only matching archetypes participate. Accessor must exactly match the registration filter, all filter types must belong to the world, and writable include/write inputs are rejected. Ordinary include/exclude/exclusive membership rules still apply. The world owns one copyable classifier value; a second registration raises. Do not mutate the world or retain accessors or references from classify.
grid_cell uses floor: -0.1 at cell width 1 becomes cell -1. Coordinates and cell width must be finite, width positive, and resulting cells in [-1048576, 1048575]. morton_key_3d biases each signed 21-bit axis and interleaves its bits into a collision-free 63-bit key, with z=0 for this planar simulation. Invalid inputs raise; they never clamp or wrap. Use an application encoding if these bounds do not fit.
data.execute-and-troubleshoot#Execute and tro:
The final driver checks negative flooring and bounds, both placement policies, staging, fixed selection membership, and positions retrieved by stable handle.
def main() raises: """Checks grid bounds, default ordering, and partitioned selections. Raises: Error: If any spatial contract check fails. """ assert_equal(grid_cell(-0.1, 1), -1) with assert_raises(): _ = grid_cell(1048576, 1) with assert_raises(): _ = morton_key_3d(0, -1048577) run_stage[False]() run_stage[True]() print("PASS: row ordering, partition staging, exact selections, and bounds") Run pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/spatial.mojo from the repository root. Its PASS covers host spatial execution, not device spatial validation.
Failure Recovery Dirty cluster selection Release old selections, finish explicit maintenance, then select again. Locked-world maintenance/selection End live queries, selections, and storage ranges, even if exhausted or empty. Invalid grid/Morton coordinate Check finite inputs, positive width and bounds; change the application encoding if needed. Unexpected placement after raw writes Mark affected live identities or fully invalidate, then maintain. Do not reuse escaped references after maintenance. The spatial reference links exact declarations; the partition benchmark records scoped measurements rather than a general speed guarantee.

data.run-movement-before-explicit-maintenance:
The movement filter and kernel stay visible alongside their classifier.
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta Movement declares Position writable, so Larecs marks eligible matching identities dirty. Read-only declarations or unrelated component writes do not invalidate classifier inputs. Values change immediately; placement waits.
Call World.maintain_spatial at the chosen boundary after execution.
@fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Moves particles and then refreshes their physical placement.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Runs explicit maintenance after movement completes. Args: context: Access to the unlocked world. Raises: Error: If execution or maintenance fails. """ context.run[move]() context.world[].maintain_spatial() Move.update waits for the synchronous kernel, then classifies dirty inputs using their final host values. Kernel completion and system completion do not invoke maintenance automatically. End every query/selection first, including empty or exhausted cursors. Discard component references before maintenance, even when you expect a clean no-op, and reacquire them by entity handle.
data.select-exact-maintained-cluster-membersh:
The driver captures key (0, 0) after maintenance, intersecting it with a component filter across logical archetypes.
comptime if partitioned: # New rows are visible to ordinary execution while still staged. var staged = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.25, 0)) assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]()]()), 4) var context = SystemContext(world) with assert_raises(): _ = context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()]( morton_key_3d(0, 0) ) world.maintain_spatial() var clean_context = SystemContext(world) var selected = clean_context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()]( morton_key_3d(0, 0) ) assert_equal( len(selected), 2 ) # walker and staged; two logical archetypes selected.run[move]() # only walker has Velocity assert_equal(len(selected), 2) # membership stays fixed after the write selected^.release() world.maintain_spatial() assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 1.5) assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](staged).x, 0.25) SystemContext.select_cluster requires partition mode, clean maintenance, and an unlocked world. Its selection initially contains walker and staged, even though only walker has Velocity and matches move. Movement changes walker’s cell, but the selection’s membership stays fixed until release; refresh placement before acquiring the next cluster selection. Even an empty result owns a structural lock. This is exact equality to the maintained key, not a radius query. Morton key adjacency does not guarantee spatial adjacency. Enumerate relevant cells and check actual distances, or build a separate spatial index, for exact neighbors.
data.track-dirty-inputs-and-choose-a-cadence#:
A maintenance pass classifies each distinct dirty eligible identity once. Repeated writes deduplicate; a clean pass scans no rows. Registration, structural changes, and full invalidation request a full rebuild. If every allocated identity is dirty, maintenance uses contiguous full classification.
Mutable storage.get[Position] marks inputs even if you only read; use read or read-only queries for observation. Setters, declared writable host/threaded ranges, and device copy-back mark affected inputs conservatively. Raw pointers or low-level storage writes bypass tracking: call world.storage.mark_spatial_dirty(entity) for each affected live identity or World.invalidate_spatial for a full rebuild. External policy changes also need full invalidation. These calls invalidate without moving rows.
Classifier errors preserve committed keys and row order and retain dirty state for retry. All fallible classification and reorder planning precedes movement; fatal allocation/lifecycle failures offer no rollback. Fix the input or policy and retry at an unlocked boundary.
Measure maintenance together with your workload. Wide component rows increase bytes moved; sparse partitions add allocations and metadata; ordinary scans pay binding/traversal per physical store. Active maintenance still copies identity-capacity keys and rebuilds a temporary cluster directory, and cluster selection scans store metadata. Structural-heavy steps request full rebuilds. A locality-sensitive pass can benefit without improving a full step; compare both complete-step costs.

data.create-entities-outside-a-system#Create: During setup, HostStorage.add_entities creates a batch directly in the world. It returns a locked row range for direct component access, not a selection, and has no run method. Inside systems, use context.add_entities to get a selection.
data.empty-and-invalid-batches#Empty and inva: add_entities with count=0 returns an empty selection that still holds a lock. Running a kernel on an empty selection never runs the kernel body. A negative count raises.
data.end-the-structural-lock-with-with#End th:
Create a batch of entities, change their components, and run kernels on only those entities with a scoped selection. Then remove entities once the scope ends. Create and remove particles runs this code and checks the result.
def reset_position(context: KernelContext[Filter().write[Position]()]): """Initializes every selected position without reading it. Args: context: Selected rows with write-only Position access. """ for particle in context: particle.set(Position(0, 0)) @fieldwise_init struct Spawn(System): """Creates and moves only the new particles at initialization.""" def initialize(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Creates a scoped batch. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If creation or movement fails. """ with context.add_entities(Position(9, 9), count=3) as selected: selected.add(Velocity(1, 0)) selected.run[reset_position]() selected.run[move]() context.world[].storage.remove_entities[ Filter().include[Position]().exclude[Velocity]() ]() def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Leaves creation to initialization. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. """ pass
context.add_entities creates three particles and returns a selection of exactly those three. Inside the with block, selected.add, selected.run, and other selection methods act on those particles only. After the block, remove_entities deletes every particle with a Position and no Velocity.
Values versus structure Assigning position.x in a kernel changes a value. Creating or deleting an entity, or adding or removing a component type, changes the world’s structure. A structural change can move rows in memory. After one, discard component references and row accessors, and look components up again by entity handle.
Select exactly the entities you change These operations return an EntitySelection:
SystemContext.add_entities selects exactly the new entities. SystemContext.add, SystemContext.remove, and SystemContext.replace select the entities that match the filter you pass. A selection keeps its members when their components change. Its add, remove, and replace methods change the members’ components in place and return nothing; remove removes components, not entities. Its run method visits the members that also match the kernel’s filter, and never other entities with the same components.
EntitySelection documents every selection method.
End the structural lock with with A selection holds a structural lock until it is released. While any lock is held, unrelated entity creation, entity deletion, and component additions or removals raise a locked-world error.
Use with so the lock ends when the block ends, including on an error or an early return. To scope a selection you already hold, write with selection^ as selected:. Inside with, the lock lasts until the block ends, even if you release the bound selection earlier. Without with, the lock ends when you call the consuming release method or the selection is destroyed. Selections are movable but not copyable.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Update entities with systems and kernels compares selections with queries and entity handles. Adding and removing entities shows the individual storage operations.
data.remove-entities#Remove entities: HostStorage.remove_entity deletes one entity by handle, and HostStorage.remove_entities deletes every entity that matches a filter. SystemContext has no method for deleting entities, so a system deletes through context.world[].storage, as Spawn does. Delete only after the with block ends; while the selection’s lock is held, deletion raises a locked-world error.

data: Larecs provides atomic scalars and scoped shared-read/exclusive-write access through AtomicValue and Synchronized. Their views share protection identity when copied; owners and acquired guards are noncopyable. This first implementation provides target-local primitives. Automatic KernelContext.sync bindings, collection domains, and deferred waiting are planned work.
data.atomic-updates#Atomic updates:
Use atomic operations for shared UInt32 and Int32 values. fetch_add and fetch_sub return the previous value and wrap at the scalar width. Strong compare_exchange returns exchanged and observed; failure changes no value through that call. A read view permits loads only.
from larecs import AtomicValue, Synchronized from std.atomic import Ordering from std.testing import assert_equal, assert_false, assert_true def main() raises: """Checks atomic updates and shared/exclusive access. Raises: Error: If an example result is incorrect. """ var counter = AtomicValue[UInt32](0) var updates = counter.write_view() assert_equal(updates.fetch_add(1), UInt32(0)) var result = updates.compare_exchange(1, 5) assert_true(result.exchanged) assert_equal(result.observed, UInt32(1)) updates.store[Ordering.RELEASE](7) assert_equal(updates.load[Ordering.ACQUIRE](), UInt32(7)) var state = Synchronized[UInt32](10) var access = state.write_view() var first_result = access.try_read() var second_result = access.try_read() assert_true(first_result.is_acquired()) assert_true(second_result.is_acquired()) var first = first_result^.take() var second = second_result^.take() assert_equal(first.value(), UInt32(10)) assert_false(access.try_write().is_acquired()) first^.release() second^.release() var writer_result = access.try_write() assert_true(writer_result.is_acquired()) var writer = writer_result^.take() writer.value() += 5 writer^.release() var after_result = access.try_read() var after = after_result^.take() assert_equal(after.value(), UInt32(15)) All public operations default to relaxed atomic ordering. Loads additionally accept acquire, stores accept release, and updates accept acquire, release, or Ordering.ACQUIRE_RELEASE. Specify ordering as a compile-time argument. Relaxed counters do not publish neighboring ordinary data. Guard operations always use acquire/release ordering internally.
data.host-and-device-use#Host and device use:
The same view methods select CPU-wide or whole-device atomic scope at compilation (NVIDIA device, AMD agent). CPU tests exercise actual parallel workers; this does not add parallel ECS system execution. Owners can be borrowed directly for host work.
Device support is experimental. Apple supports relaxed or acquire loads, relaxed or release stores, and relaxed add/subtract. Release stores followed by acquire loads publish ordinary payload writes across thread blocks. Strong CAS, ordered add/subtract, and guards fail with explicit diagnostics. CPU/NVIDIA/AMD use the full initial operation set. GPU compilation probes do not establish actual hardware correctness.
Device payloads, counters, and lock state must already reside in aligned device-accessible memory. The keyword-only AtomicView(unsafe_pointer=...) and SyncView(unsafe_payload=..., unsafe_state=...) constructors are low-level adapters: the caller guarantees lifetime, alignment, atomic-only scalar access, and one initialized canonical lock state for every overlapping payload. They do not allocate, transfer data, or validate a host pointer’s device accessibility. Guard state must be initialized unlocked before launch and remain live until all work completes.
Ordinary raw-byte resource/capture checks reject these views and aggregates containing them: their explicit move/destruction methods prevent treating them as transferable host pointers. Those paths do not transfer referenced storage or encode synchronization ownership. Dedicated binding adapters remain unfinished. CPU and GPU allocations are separate domains; this API does not permit concurrent CPU/GPU access to one allocation. Backend compilation evidence and hardware limitations are recorded in decision 0016.
data.scoped-access-and-contention#Scoped acce:
Multiple read guards can coexist; a write guard excludes all other guards for its domain. try_read() and try_write() make at most one compare-exchange attempt and return TryAccess. Check is_acquired() before consuming the result with result^.take(). False represents Busy, including a changed state or reader-count saturation. Acquiring a guard does not allocate memory.
guard.value() lends a reference tied to the guard. The compiler rejects using it after release or moving its owner while the borrow remains live. Scope exit releases the guard, including error unwinding. guard^.release() explicitly consumes and releases it; consuming an acquired result without extracting its guard also releases access. A write error does not roll back partial mutation.
Copies of one view refer to the same payload and state. Read views do not permit write acquisition. Do not access private fields or create separate state words for overlapping payloads. Heap-backed payloads additionally require a consistent protection contract for all mutable reachable storage.
There is no fairness, blocking wait, lock upgrade, or automatic retry. Handle Busy by recording unfinished work or using an application-approved skip. Do not assume skipping is valid for required updates. The proposed deferred API is not implemented, and ordinary statements do not suspend on contention.

data:
Put repeated simulation work in a system, and let the system run a kernel over every entity that matches a filter. This page uses the movement code from Your first simulation.
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Advances every particle by its velocity times the step length. Args: context: The matching rows and the declared resources. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Runs the `move` kernel once per step.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Moves all particles. Args: context: Access to the scheduler's world. Raises: Error: If `Time` is missing from the world. """ context.run[move]() var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=10)
move is the kernel, Move is the system that runs it, and the Scheduler calls Move.update once per step.
data.compare-handles-queries-and-selections#C: Value Copy and move Structural lock Use Entity handle Copyable and movable None Identify an entity in storage calls; survives row movement, not deletion Query row accessor Movable, not copyable Held by its query Read the query’s components; discard before structural changes Query Copy: own cursor and lock. Move: transfers the lock Until destroyed, even when exhausted or empty Read-only traversal Entity selection Movable, not copyable Until released, destroyed, or its with block ends, even when empty Change components and run kernels on exactly its members Storage batch range (HostStorage.add_entities) Copy: own cursor and lock. Move: transfers the lock Until destroyed, even when exhausted or empty Low-level traversal and mutable unsafe_get; no run Create and remove entities in batches covers selections.
data.declare-component-and-resource-access#De:
A Filter selects entities and sets how the kernel may access their components:
Step Matches Access through the kernel include[T]() Entities with T Read and write with get read[T]() Entities with T Read with get write[T]() Entities with T Write with set only exclude[T]() Entities without T None exclusive() Only entities without further components Unchanged The kernel’s KernelContext exposes only the declared access. Calling get on a component the filter does not guarantee, or writing through read access, fails to compile. Resources declares resource access separately; see Share values with resources.
data.how-often-a-kernel-runs#How often a kern: On the host, SystemContext.run calls the kernel once for each non-empty matching physical store: a group of rows with the same components. One logical archetype can have several physical stores. Put per-entity work inside the for loop over the context. With no matching entities, the kernel body never runs. All calls finish before run returns, so the next system sees the results.
data.inspect-entities-outside-a-kernel#Inspec:
Use HostStorage.query to read entities outside a kernel, for example during setup. Create and remove particles inspects the marker before it starts the scheduler:
var query = world.storage.query[ Filter().read[Position]().exclude[Velocity]() ]() var query_copy = query.copy() for row in query^: assert_almost_equal(row.get[Position]().x, -3.0) assert_equal(row.get_entity(), marker) for _ in query_copy^: pass assert_equal( len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]().exclusive()]()), 1 ) Each query row is an ArchetypeRowAccessor, not an entity handle. get reads a component the filter guarantees, and get_entity returns the entity’s handle. A query is read-only, even when its filter uses include; use a kernel to change values. exclusive() restricts a query to entities with exactly the listed components, so the last assertion counts only marker.
A live query holds a structural lock, even after it is exhausted or when it matched nothing. Consume it in a short loop, or let it go out of scope, before you create or remove entities. A copy starts at the same position with its own cursor and lock; a move transfers the existing lock. The example copies the query to show this, and consumes both with ^ so their locks end before the scheduler takes the world. Do not keep a row accessor beyond its query or across structural changes. Structural locks protect references from invalidation; they are not thread mutexes.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Execution covers captures, portable resources, threaded host kernels, and device execution. HostStorage and ArchetypeRowAccessor document lower-level traversal.
data.order-systems-and-steps#Order systems an:
System has three hooks: initialize, update, and finalize. Scheduler.run initializes all systems, updates them once per step, and then finalizes them. Within each phase, systems run in the order you added them.
An error in a hook propagates out of run, and run does not guarantee that finalize runs afterwards. To step the simulation in several batches, call initialize, update(steps=...), and finalize yourself.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause and fix run raises about a missing resource The kernel declares a resource the world lacks. Add it during setup. Compile error on component access The filter does not guarantee the component, or grants only read access. Adjust the filter. Locked-world error A query or selection is still alive. End its scope before the structural change.
data.write-values-without-reading-them#Write:
def reset_position(context: KernelContext[Filter().write[Position]()]): """Initializes every selected position without reading it. Args: context: Selected rows with write-only Position access. """ for particle in context: particle.set(Position(0, 0)) Filter.write permits EntityAccessor.set and rejects get. Set the component on every row the kernel visits; a later kernel can then read it. Create and remove particles runs this kernel before movement.
For device execution, the access mode decides the transfers: read access uploads values, write access downloads results, and read-write access does both. Write-only values are not uploaded. See device execution for target limits.

data: In an entity component system, you organize the operations on entities in systems. You register each system with a Scheduler, which runs its lifecycle methods for all registered systems in registration order. Registration is permanent: the scheduler has no method to remove a system.
data.capturing-host-kernels#Capturing host ke:
Pass a closure as an argument to context.run(kernel) to borrow surrounding values on the host. Use imm for read-only captures and mut for values the kernel updates. Capturing kernels may also declare required resources.
from larecs import World, SystemContext, KernelContext, Filter, Resources, ResourceType from std.testing import assert_equal @fieldwise_init struct Offset(ResourceType): var value: Int32 def main() raises: var world = World[Int32]() world.resources.add(Offset(2)) var entity = world.storage.add_entity(Int32(4)) var factor: Int32 = 3 var visits = 0 def scale_rows( rows: KernelContext[Filter().include[Int32](), Resources[Offset]()] ) {imm factor, mut visits}: """Updates matching rows and counts visits. Args: rows: Components and resources available to the kernel. """ for row in rows: row.get[Int32]() = row.get[Int32]() * factor + rows.resources.get[Offset]().value visits += 1 var context = SystemContext(world) context.run(scale_rows) assert_equal(visits, 1) assert_equal(world.storage.get[Int32](entity), 14) Execution is synchronous: changes to mutable captures are visible after run returns. The kernel runs once per matching dense physical store and visits only that store’s rows. With partitioned spatial storage, each block contributes a separate host invocation. Do not structurally modify the world from a captured alias while those rows are being processed.
data.device-execution#Device execution:
The host is the CPU running the system and managing ECS storage; the device is the GPU accelerator running the launched kernel. Host/device describes their execution and memory roles. Import the target enum with from larecs import ExecutionBackend and select backend=ExecutionBackend.HOST or backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE.
The SystemContext.run call used by Move executes its kernel on the host by default. Pass backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE to run a compatible kernel on an accelerator. The same kernel function works on both targets unchanged; see the SystemContext.run and KernelContext API docs for details. Device execution requires an available accelerator and the corresponding Mojo GPU toolchain. Selecting DEVICE raises an error when accelerator compilation support or a working world device context is unavailable, including for empty matches. There is no automatic backend selection or host fallback.
backend is a compile-time parameter on both SystemContext.run and EntitySelection.run. This specializes kernel compilation and transfer checks for the chosen target. Runtime choices require an explicit branch calling each specialization. Thin compile-time kernels support both targets; value-taking callables (including lexical closures) require HOST, checked at compile time. threaded=True requires HOST and a thin kernel.
Migrate on_device=True (formerly on_gpu=True) to backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE, and on_device=False / on_gpu=False to backend=ExecutionBackend.HOST or omit the parameter for the host default. Boolean parameters are removed without compatibility aliases. Applications that previously relied on the no-accelerator fallback must choose HOST explicitly when device support is unavailable.
Required resources use the same context.resources.get[T]() API on the device. Resource transfer constraints, shared-write safety, and the non-capturing kernel requirement are covered in Resources.
Each device run uploads the components and resources it reads. Worlds that opt into world.reuse_device_copies(True) (experimental) skip uploading unchanged resources and component column ranges; this requires re-obtaining references after runs or invalidating device copies explicitly. See Reusing unchanged device copies.
Use explicit bindings above to pass host-local values to device entry points; lexical host borrows are not transferred automatically. Nested closures inside a device kernel can capture that thread’s kernel-local variables with imm and mut. Each thread owns its local values; updating a local capture does not update a variable on the host or communicate with other GPU threads.
data.passing-host-local-values-to-a-device-ke:
Declare explicit capture slots with Captures, using ReadCapture for inputs and MutCapture for values that must be copied back. Bind host locals with read_capture and mut_capture when calling run. Inside the kernel, context.captures.get[index]() returns a reference with the declared access. The slot index is compile-time; two slots may have the same value type.
from larecs import ( ExecutionBackend, World, SystemContext, KernelContext, Filter, Captures, ReadCapture, MutCapture, read_capture, mut_capture, ) from std.sys import has_accelerator from std.gpu import global_idx from std.sys.info import is_gpu from std.testing import assert_equal comptime locals_spec = Captures[ReadCapture[Int32], MutCapture[Int32]]() def scale( context: KernelContext[Filter().include[Int32](), capture_spec=locals_spec] ): """Scales components and reports the number of processed entities. Args: context: Matching rows and the explicitly bound host-local values. """ for entity in context: entity.get[Int32]() *= context.captures.get[0]() # The output is shared by all threads: only one GPU thread updates it. comptime if is_gpu(): if global_idx.x != 0: return context.captures.get[1]() += context.length def main() raises: """Demonstrates input transfer and synchronous copy-back. Raises: Error: If setup, execution, or a result check fails. """ comptime if not has_accelerator(): return var world = World[Int32]() var entity = world.storage.add_entity(Int32(4)) var factor: Int32 = 3 var processed: Int32 = 0 var context = SystemContext(world) context.run[scale, backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]( read_capture(factor), mut_capture(processed) ) assert_equal(world.storage.get[Int32](entity), 12) assert_equal(processed, 1) Each invocation uploads the current bound values. Mutable slots are shared device allocations, and their final values are copied back to the original host locals before run returns. Read-only slots are not downloaded and cannot be written through get. Empty matches leave captures unchanged. Captures need no entry in the world’s resource storage and can coexist with required resources.
Binding count, value types, and mutability must match the declaration. Bindings borrow their locals, so the borrow checker rejects conflicting read-only and mutable bindings to the same value. Neither a capture reference nor its pointer may escape the kernel invocation.
Device captures currently support trivially copyable, trivially deletable values, such as numbers and plain structs. They copy bytes, not object graphs: List, Dict, host-backed tensors, and pointers to host-only memory cannot be transferred this way. DevicePassable conversion is not performed for capture values. Writes to a mutable capture must use a single writer or appropriate synchronization/atomics, just like writes to shared resources.
The same explicit bindings work with host kernels, including the closure overload. Host execution borrows the original values directly and calls the kernel once per matching physical store (each spatial partition block when enabled); device execution processes the matching rows in one launch. In the example, adding context.length once per host store or once for the device launch gives the same total.
data.resources-in-kernels#Resources in kernel: Systems may access the world’s resource storage directly through context.world[].resources, for example when adding a resource during initialize. The example above adds Time before Move runs and declares it in the kernel’s Resources[Time]() list. See Resources for the complete kernel API, missing-resource behavior, mutation semantics, and runnable examples.
data.systems#Systems:
Systems are the principal way to mutate the state of the ECS. Application logic that creates or removes entities, changes components, or updates resources should generally live in a system, where the scheduler can run it in a defined order with access to the appropriate context.
Systems are structs implementing the System trait, so they can retain state between calls. A system implements update, which is called at every step of the ECS run. It can also override the default no-op initialize and finalize methods, which run before and after the update loop.
Each lifecycle method receives a SystemContext. Its world field provides access to entities, components, and resources for individual or structural changes. For component processing across every entity matching a filter, the system calls SystemContext.run with a kernel. A kernel is a function that receives a KernelContext; it is not itself a system and is not registered with the scheduler.
from larecs import ( ExecutionBackend, World, System, SystemContext, KernelContext, Filter, Resources, ResourceType, ) @fieldwise_init struct Position(Movable, Copyable, TrivialRegisterPassable): var x: Float64 var y: Float64 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Movable, Copyable, TrivialRegisterPassable): var dx: Float64 var dy: Float64 @fieldwise_init struct Time(ResourceType, TrivialRegisterPassable): var delta: Float64 # This kernel writes Position and reads Velocity for every matching entity. # Move.update invokes it through the system's SystemContext below. comptime move_resources = Resources[Time]() def move_entities( context: KernelContext[ Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity](), move_resources ] ): ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for entity in context: ref pos = entity.get[Position]() ref vel = entity.get[Velocity]() pos.x += vel.dx * time.delta pos.y += vel.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): # This is executed once at the beginning def initialize(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: # We do not need to do anything here pass # This is executed in each step def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: # Move all entities with a position and velocity context.run[move_entities]() # This is executed at the end def finalize(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: # We do not need to do anything here pass Note
SystemContext[...] uses ... to let the compiler infer the context’s world origin and component types from where the system is used, rather than spelling them out. The world field is a Pointer, so it must be dereferenced (context.world[]) to reach the world itself.
data.threaded-host-execution-experimental#Thr:
Configure a fixed worker-task budget on the world and explicitly opt in per run:
from larecs import World, SystemContext, KernelContext, Filter, ThreadedExecutionConfig def increment_threaded(rows: KernelContext[Filter().include[Int32]()]): """Increments each row in one prepared range. Args: rows: Disjoint host range with chunk-local indices. """ for row in rows: row.get[Int32]() += 1 def threaded_example() raises: """Runs the same kernel sequentially and on the shared CPU runtime. Raises: Error: If configuration or execution preparation fails. """ var world = World[Int32]( execution_config=ThreadedExecutionConfig(workers=4) ) _ = world.storage.add_entities(Int32(0), count=65_536) var context = SystemContext(world) context.run[increment_threaded, threaded=True]() context.run[increment_threaded]() ThreadedExecutionConfig() defaults to one worker, four target chunks per worker, and a 65,536 matched-row cutoff. Custom construction requires workers; chunks_per_worker and min_parallel_rows are optional. Worker and chunk counts must be positive, the cutoff nonnegative, and their product representable. min_parallel_rows=0 disables the row cutoff. Invalid settings raise an error. World.execution_config() returns a copy; idle world copies/moves retain the policy. MAX owns the shared runtime: the budget bounds submitted tasks, without reserving cores or promising that many simultaneous OS threads.
Both SystemContext.run[kernel, threaded=True]() and EntitySelection.run[kernel, threaded=True]() support the same engine. Each physical store or exact selected range is split independently, including partition/staging stores; selected gaps remain untouched. Workers claim jobs dynamically. Each row executes once, and the call joins all workers before returning. Systems and successive kernel calls retain their sequential order.
Ordinary calls keep existing whole-range sequential behavior. Explicit threaded calls also use whole ranges when there is one worker or fewer matched rows than the cutoff, after validating threaded eligibility. Empty matches invoke no kernel. Only parallel dispatch introduces chunking: invocation order is unspecified, local indices restart in each chunk, and code outside the entity loop runs once per chunk. Kernels must tolerate these changes when the cutoff or worker settings change; cross-chunk dependencies require a later run. KernelContext.thread_count remains one within each host chunk; it does not report the configured worker-task budget.
The initial engine accepts nonraising thin kernels, pointer-free plain-value accessed components, and explicit Resources().read[T]() resources. Reflection cannot inspect StaticTuple or InlineArray storage, so a type holding such a field of scalars must conform to PlainValue to declare that it holds no pointers; Larecs trusts the declaration. Ordinary read resources must also be plain values; heap-backed resources use adapter views, bound once on the caller and shared until join. Adapted resources may be declared write or read_write when their adapter declares supports_concurrent_mutation; see mutable adapted resources. Unaccessed owning components do not prevent threading. Other mutable resources (including the legacy Resources[T]() default), explicit captures, lexical closures, and threaded=True with backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE are rejected even on fallback.
Every explicitly threaded call acquires an additional structural lock, including whole-range fallback and calls on an already locked selection. Exhausting the world’s lock slots raises before execution; the selection’s own lock remains held. Ordinary sequential calls retain their existing lock behavior.
Keep the world confined to one coordinating caller. Reentrant execution and structural mutation during a threaded call are rejected; copying, moving, replacing, or destroying an active world aborts. Escaped aliases must not mutate resource backing data or invalidate component storage. Avoid mutable globals and non-thread-safe callees: signature and representation checks cannot prove an arbitrary kernel safe. Overlapping selected ranges are rejected before dispatch. All fallible preparation completes before spatial invalidation and row writes; fatal worker/runtime failures have no recovery or rollback guarantee.
Linux correctness tests exercise actual worker overlap. The overlap check uses a Python test probe to skip hosts with fewer than two available CPUs, accounting for process affinity and inherited Linux cgroup v1/v2 CPU quotas. Fractional quotas round down; a skip does not establish concurrency coverage. macOS arm64 validation and performance measurements remain pending, so this engine is experimental.

Larecs🌲 is a performance-oriented archetype-based ECS for Mojo.
It is based on the ECS Arche, implemented in the Go programming language.
Larecs 1.0 is currently in beta, so public APIs may still change before the stable 1.0.0 release. After that release, public APIs follow semantic versioning unless they are explicitly marked experimental. Device execution is currently such an experimental API. Threaded host execution is also experimental.

def reserve(mut self) Doubles the current capacity (minimum 8) to provide exponential growth that minimizes the frequency of memory reallocations while maintaining reasonable memory usage. This follows standard container growth patterns optimized for amortized performance.
Args:

def reserve(mut self, new_capacity: Int) Uses a power-of-2 allocation strategy to ensure optimal memory alignment and reduce fragmentation. The actual allocated capacity will be the next power of 2 greater than or equal to the requested capacity.
Does nothing if the requested capacity is not larger than the current capacity, avoiding unnecessary work and maintaining existing memory layout.

data.aliases#Aliases:
ComponentType The trait that components must conform to.
ComponentType = Copyable & Deinitable DeviceComponentType Trait subset of ComponentType safe for device raw-byte transfer.
DeviceComponentType = TrivialRegisterPassable SystemContext.run(..., backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE) moves component columns between host and device buffers via a plain byte copy (see DeviceComponentStorage): the destination never runs T’s copy constructor or destructor, only memcpys its bytes. That is only sound for a type with no non-trivial state – no owned heap allocation, no custom copy/move/destroy logic – since a bitwise copy of such a type would corrupt or leak it. TrivialRegisterPassable already encodes exactly that constraint at the type-system level (bitwise copyable, trivially destroyed, and transitively so for every member), so it is reused here rather than inventing a new marker trait.
It also already implies Copyable & Deinitable (i.e. ComponentType), so it alone is the constraint – composing it with ComponentType would be redundant.

data.filter#\u003ccode\u003eFilter\u003c/code:
Development reference · Larecs 1.0.0b1 · revision 24a607075a78. Host threading and device execution are experimental. Compatibility and status.
Mojo structSource
Filter @memory_only struct Filter[_include: Components[_include.ComponentTypes] = Components(), _exclude: Components[_exclude.ComponentTypes] = Components(), _is_exclusive: Bool = False, _read: Components[_read.ComponentTypes] = Components(), _written: Components[_written.ComponentTypes] = Components()] Compile-time component inclusion and exclusion spec used to build queries.
Every included component is tracked separately as readable (_read) and/or writable (_written). include – the default, and the only mode that matters for the host query API, where this distinction is not used – marks a component both readable and writable, matching this type’s behavior before _read/_written existed. read and write mark a component for one direction only: a kernel running on the device then only pays for the transfer direction it actually needs (see SystemContext.run), and EntityAccessor.get/set enforce the declared mode at compile time, not just by convention – see read and write below.
Build a filter by chaining include, read, write, exclude, and exclusive, then call the result, as in Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity](). Each step names a new Filter type; the trailing () constructs the filter value that queries and kernels take. Without it, the compiler reports failed to infer parameter '_include'. Calling every step, as in Filter().include[Position]().exclude[Velocity](), builds the same filter.
A named filter can be extended, which lets several systems share a base filter:
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable): var x: Float64 var y: Float64 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable): var dx: Float64 var dy: Float64 @fieldwise_init struct Frozen(Copyable, Movable): pass comptime moving = Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity]() comptime moving_unfrozen = moving.exclude[Frozen]() def main() raises: var world = World[Position, Velocity, Frozen]() _ = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) _ = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0), Frozen()) assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[moving]()), 2) assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[moving_unfrozen]()), 1)

EntityAccessorIterator @memory_only struct EntityAccessorIterator[filter: Filter[filter._include, filter._exclude, filter._is_exclusive, filter._read, filter._written]] Iterates filtered component rows with host or device-appropriate strides.
The iterator does not enumerate entity IDs or archetypes. It walks the dense rows described by KernelContext and yields an EntityAccessor containing a row offset and one byte-addressed pointer per included component. The accessor’s get and set methods use the filter’s compile-time component order to select a column, then use the row offset to access that column’s structure-of-arrays (SoA) element.
On the host, iteration starts at row 0 and advances by 1. The context therefore describes one homogeneous component range, normally a single matching archetype. On a device, is_gpu() removes the host path at compile time: each thread starts at global_idx.x and advances by the total number of threads in the launch. This gives every thread the rows global_idx.x, global_idx.x + thread_count, and so on, while the bounds check stops at context.length.
The same kernel source is consequently valid on both targets. Host contexts contain host pointers, while the device-passable host context is converted to device pointers before a device launch. The iterator itself performs no host/device copy or synchronization; callers must ensure the columns are initialized, have at least context.length rows, and that each row is written by at most one concurrent thread.

LockedEntityRange @memory_only struct LockedEntityRange[archetype_list_mutability: Bool, //, archetype_list_origin: Origin[mut=archetype_list_mutability], lock_origin: MutOrigin, *ComponentTypes: ComponentType, *, row_filter: Filter[row_filter._include, row_filter._exclude, row_filter._is_exclusive, row_filter._read, row_filter._written] = Filter(), has_ranges: Bool = False] Storage-borrowing row range with an independent cursor and structural guard.
Returned by queries and low-level batch mutations. Query access is read-only; mutation results permit mutable setup access. System logic uses EntitySelection.run instead. Explicit range metadata and query archetype indices are immutable and shared across cursor copies.
Acquires the lock before initializing traversal and releases it on destruction, including early loop exits. Moving the wrapper transfers ownership of the lock without acquiring another one. Copying preserves the traversal position and acquires a distinct lock; it aborts if no lock is available. Exhaustion does not release the lock while the wrapper is still alive.
This is not a thread-synchronization mutex. The lock prevents structural changes to the world, not component reads or writes. The underlying iterator is kept private so traversal always happens while locked.

data.entitypool#\u003ccode\u003eEntityPool\u0:
Development reference · Larecs 1.0.0b1 · revision 24a607075a78. Host threading and device execution are experimental. Compatibility and status.
Mojo structSource
EntityPool @memory_only struct EntityPool EntityPool is an implementation using implicit linked lists.
Follows the entity recycling scheme from ECS back and forth, part 3.
Per-ID generations survive reset. Recycling or resetting advances the affected generations modulo 232; an ancient handle can alias a new one after 232 advances of its ID. Handles are local to a pool, and copying a pool creates an independent snapshot with the same handles and history. Copying takes O(high-water mark) time and storage, including retained IDs.

data.resourceadapter#\u003ccode\u003eResource:
Development reference · Larecs 1.0.0b1 · revision 24a607075a78. Host threading and device execution are experimental. Compatibility and status.
Mojo traitSource
ResourceAdapterStateless operations over the current source; no factory or adapter instance.
View[False] is the read view and View[True] the mutable view; they may be distinct types. Descriptors are immutable trivial values: mutable views reach shared state through pointers into adapter-managed backing buffers.
Views and their pointers must not escape a synchronous invocation. Every read view must support concurrent reads on its execution target, including view methods and all reachable data, without hidden unsafe mutation. No alias may mutate, resize, relocate, or free backing data before completion. The adapter author guarantees this; descriptor checks cannot prove it. Device preparation must transfer through ResourceDeviceCache, never enqueue a copy from an external host pointer. Validation must neither mutate nor queue work.
Mutable access is opt-in. supports_mutation admits write and read_write declarations on sequential host execution. GPU and threaded host execution additionally require supports_concurrent_mutation, which the author may declare only if every mutable view operation is safe under concurrent use, for example through atomics or provably disjoint writes. Larecs’s exclusive source lease does not prevent races among kernel workers; the user is responsible for safe resource access.

ResourceDeviceCache @memory_only struct ResourceDeviceCache Reuses allocations for one source type on one world’s device queue.
Adapter transfers must use this cache’s staging helpers. A slot identifies one contiguous allocation; nonnegative slots belong to the adapter. Slot -1 is reserved by Larecs for the view descriptor. Scheduler @memory_only struct Scheduler[*ComponentTypes: ComponentType] Manages the execution of systems in a world.
The systems must implement System. run initializes the systems in registration order, updates them in the same order once per step, and finalizes them after the last step.
Example:
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable): var x: Float64 var y: Float64 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable): var dx: Float64 var dy: Float64 # A system delegates filtered component processing to a kernel like this. comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity]() def move_entities(context: KernelContext[move_filter]): for entity in context: ref pos = entity.get[Position]() ref vel = entity.get[Velocity]() pos.x += vel.dx pos.y += vel.dy @fieldwise_init struct MySystem(System): var internal_variable: Int # This is executed once at the beginning def initialize(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: _ = context.world[].storage.add_entities( Position(0.0, 0.0), Velocity(1.0, 1.0), count=10 ) # This is executed in each step def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: context.run[move_entities]() # This is executed at the end def finalize(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: print("Final positions") for entity in context.world[].storage.query[Filter().include[Position]()](): print(entity.get[Position]().x, entity.get[Position]().y) def main() raises: var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity]() scheduler.add_system(MySystem(internal_variable=42)) scheduler.run(10)

EntitySelection @memory_only struct EntitySelection[world_origin: MutOrigin, *WorldTs: ComponentType] Owns exact entity row ranges and one structural-change lock.
A selection borrows its world, is movable and noncopyable, and keeps the world structurally locked until release, destruction, or scope exit. A with block retains the guard and lends a scope-bound selection that supports the same kernels and in-place mutations. Kernel runs borrow a selection; component mutations update its membership in place while retaining the same guard.

def run[filter: Filter, required_resources: Resources = Resources(), capture_spec: Captures = Captures(), //, KernelFunc: def(KernelContext[filter, required_resources, capture_spec]) thin -> None, *Bindings: CaptureBindingType, *, backend: ExecutionBackend = ExecutionBackend.HOST, threaded: Bool = False](mut self, *bindings: *Bindings.values) Exact declaration def run[filter: Filter[filter._include, filter._exclude, filter._is_exclusive, filter._read, filter._written], required_resources: Resources[required_resources.ResourceTypes, _readonly=required_resources._readonly, _writeonly=required_resources._writeonly] = Resources(), capture_spec: Captures[capture_spec.Specs] = Captures(), //, KernelFunc: def(KernelContext[filter, required_resources, capture_spec]) thin -> None, *Bindings: CaptureBindingType, *, backend: ExecutionBackend = ExecutionBackend.HOST, threaded: Bool = False](mut self, *bindings: *Bindings.values) Common call forms, for a kernel function move that takes a KernelContext:
context.run[move](): run on the host, sequentially. context.run[move, threaded=True](): run on the host in concurrent chunks (experimental). context.run[move, backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE](): run on an accelerator (experimental). context.run[move](read_capture(x), mut_capture(y)): pass host-local values to a kernel that declares captures. filter, required_resources, and capture_spec are inferred from the kernel’s KernelContext parameter. The tutorial Your first simulation shows a complete program.
Execution: The call returns after all kernel work has finished.
Host: KernelFunc is called once per non-empty physical store matching filter, one store after the other. Each KernelContext iterates that store’s rows; row indices are local to the context. Threaded host: each matching store is split into chunks, and chunks may run concurrently on the world’s ThreadedExecutionConfig. With one worker or fewer matching rows than min_parallel_rows, the stores run sequentially. Device: one launch covers all matching rows. Readable columns and resources are uploaded when the device copy is not current; write-only columns are not uploaded, so the kernel must set them for every row. Written columns, read-write resources, and mutable captures are copied back before run returns. DEVICE never falls back to HOST. Access: include grants read-write component access, read read-only, and write set-only access; required_resources declares resource access the same way. Undeclared components and resources are rejected at compile time.
Empty matches: no kernel call happens. With DEVICE, the device storage and required resources are still validated, in that order, and a missing accelerator still raises.

data.api-scope-and-imports#API scope and impo:
Use root imports such as from larecs import World, Filter, SystemContext for application code. The root export list in the generated package index is checked against the initializer’s actual imports during every build. Module-qualified names remain available in the generated module tree.
Surface Intended use Application APIs World, Entity, Filter, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, KernelContext, EntitySelection, Resources and the optional APIs linked above Supported lower-level APIs HostStorage, row accessors, EntityRange, ResourceStorage, component/resource traits and documented direct storage operations Implementation utilities Store allocation, component managers, device storage, lock managers, pools and transfer caches; these explain implementation mechanisms and are not the recommended application workflow Classification does not remove existing imports or compatibility commitments. A generated declaration’s presence alone does not make it a recommended application entry point. Prefer systems and kernels for updates and scoped selections for structural batches; use direct storage for setup and individual operations.

data:
This reference describes the development checkout, currently Larecs 1.0 beta. Public APIs may change before stable 1.0.0. After stable release, public APIs follow semantic versioning unless explicitly experimental. Threaded host and device execution, mutable resource adapters, and device-copy reuse are experimental.
Contract Sequential host Threaded host Device Thin kernel Supported; default threaded=True backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE Value-taking callable Supported, including lexical captures Rejected at compile time Rejected at compile time Components Host ComponentType, including nontrivial ownership Pointer-free trivial plain values TrivialRegisterPassable transfer check Ordinary resources Host resource traits; declared access Explicit read-only pointer-free plain values Recursively checked pointer-free plain values Adapted resources Access-selected host views Mutable views require concurrent-mutation support Access-selected device views and adapter-managed transfers Explicit captures Read-only and mutable slots Unsupported Device-safe values and synchronous copy-back Scheduling One invocation per nonempty matching store Concurrent chunks; sequential below threshold or with one worker One launch across matching rows Completion Synchronous Synchronous Synchronous, including written data copied back Eligibility checks run independently of threaded worker count and fallback thresholds. Setting one worker does not allow nontrivial components, mutable ordinary resources, or captures through the threaded path. Device selection never falls back to host.
The defining contracts are SystemContext.run, component.constrain_device_safe_components, resource.constrain_device_safe_resources, and DevicePassableResource. Adapter-backed sources control their view and transfer lifecycle; a component’s device eligibility does not establish a resource’s eligibility.
Readable device data uploads when the cached copy is stale. Write-only columns skip upload and must be fully written. Read-only reuse therefore depends on revision tracking, not merely on calling the same kernel again.
Device-copy reuse is off by default and never skips written output copy-back. Standalone atomic/guard primitives exist, with Apple device restrictions; automatic kernel synchronization bindings and deferred retries are unimplemented. The execution guides keep each restriction beside its checked stage.

Read each generated operation’s Raises and Constraints before handling a failure. Constraints reject invalid programs at compile time; runtime errors report invalid state or execution failures.
API or condition Meaning and response LarecsError Variant containing typed ECS errors and general Error failures. Inspect the specific error rather than assuming every failure is an invalid entity. EntityError, ComponentError Invalid/stale entity or component membership errors. Recheck the handle generation and requested composition. WorldError Includes structural lock exhaustion, a locked world and negative batch counts. Release queries/selections before structural changes; pass a nonnegative count. Device setup or synchronization failure run raises; it does not retry on host. Fix device availability or explicitly select HOST. Invalid resource/capture access Check declarations, presence, access modes and binding order. Synchronization cannot repair a declaration mismatch. Threaded resources require explicit read access Ordinary threaded resources must declare read; mutable adapters need concurrent-mutation support. See threaded restrictions. Cluster selection requires clean spatial maintenance Release live selections/queries and maintain explicitly before selecting the next cluster. See spatial recovery. Device reads stale data with reuse enabled Reacquire mutable references after each run or invalidate after escaped writes. See copy-reuse recovery. TryAccess.is_acquired() is false The guard attempt is Busy. Record required unfinished work for a later pass; there is no automatic retry. See shared-write alternatives. A failing kernel call is not a transaction: do not infer rollback of writes already performed. Scoped selections release locks on exit, including exceptional exit. Failure effects specific to an operation remain in its defining declaration.
data.migration-spellings#Migration spellings:
Older examples may use direct World entity operations or boolean execution-target flags. Current single-entity setup uses world.storage; scheduled application updates use SystemContext. Select targets with backend=ExecutionBackend.HOST or backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE. Consult SystemContext.run for the current overloads.
The changelog records release changes. The development reference does not imply that an unreleased declaration exists in a previously installed package.

data:
SystemContext.run executes a kernel synchronously. For a complete thin kernel named move, use context.run[move](). The first simulation defines its filter, components, resource, system and scheduler.
Call form Behavior context.run[move]() Default sequential host execution; one kernel call per matching nonempty physical store. context.run[move, threaded=True]() Experimental host chunks; eligibility checks still apply when configuration selects sequential execution. context.run[move, backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() Experimental accelerator execution. No host fallback; missing hardware raises even for empty matches. context.run(kernel_func) Value-taking callable overload; lexical host captures are allowed, but the target must be sequential HOST. context.run[move](read_capture(x), mut_capture(y)) Thin kernel with explicitly declared capture slots; bindings must follow the declared order. The generated run entry keeps overload anchors, access constraints, preparation errors, and both readable and exact compiler declarations. Read the compatibility matrix before changing targets.
API Contract System Implement update; optionally implement initialize and finalize. Scheduler Owns the world and registered systems; run(steps) initializes, updates for the requested steps, and finalizes. Individual lifecycle methods are also available. KernelContext Borrows the current component/resource view; iterate it for row access. Row indices are local to each context. ExecutionBackend Compile-time HOST or DEVICE; HOST is the default. ThreadedExecutionConfig Worker/chunk settings and minimum row threshold; configuration alone does not enable threading. See Execution for independent particle stages and target restrictions. Kernels cannot perform arbitrary structural changes while execution holds structural locks.

World owns the component storage and shared resource storage for a fixed compile-time component type pack. Use World[Position, Velocity]() during setup, then pass world^ to Scheduler to transfer ownership. The first simulation supplies the complete definitions and an asserted result.
API Contract and common form Entity A handle containing an ID and generation; retain handles rather than row addresses across structural changes. get_id() alone does not establish identity after recycling. HostStorage.is_alive world.storage.is_alive(entity) checks whether the generation still names a live entity. HostStorage.add_entity world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) creates an entity and returns its handle. HostStorage.get world.storage.get[Position](entity) borrows an existing component. Adding, removing or migrating entities can invalidate row references. HostStorage.set Replace an existing component value without changing the component set. HostStorage.replace world.storage.replace[Removed]().by(value, entity=entity) changes the component set. component.ComponentType Required component traits; host components can own nontrivial data. Heap ownership adds allocation and lifecycle costs. The generated type pages retain exact constructor declarations and overloads. The compatibility table distinguishes host component support from device transfer eligibility.

Filter combines membership and kernel permissions at compile time. The common form Filter().include[Position].read[Velocity]() requires Position and Velocity, grants read-write access to Position, and grants read-only access to Velocity. The trailing () constructs the final filter value.
API Contract Filter.include, Filter.read, Filter.write Include component types with read-write, read-only or set-only access. A write-only kernel must initialize every selected output row. Filter.exclude, Filter.exclusive Exclude listed types, or match exactly the included composition. exclusive resets earlier exclusions; its generated declaration describes composition. HostStorage.query world.storage.query[filter]() creates a read-only query holding a structural lock. Release it before structural mutations. ArchetypeRowAccessor A borrowed row view; get_entity() returns a durable handle. Component references remain tied to the row and storage lifetime. EntityRange A physical store index, first row, and row count; it describes a bounded interval, not a list of handles. SystemContext.add_entities with context.add_entities[Position](count) as selected: creates an exact scoped selection. Negative counts raise; zero creates an empty selection. EntitySelection.run Runs only the selection’s retained ranges. Exiting the scope releases its structural locks, including when the body raises. Queries inspect rows; kernels mutate components according to their filter. Selections restrict kernel work to the rows returned by the structural operation. See queries and iteration for complete examples and query copy/move behavior.

ResourceStorage stores one shared value per resource type. Add values during setup with world.resources.add(Time(0.25)). Declare a kernel’s access with Resources, for example Resources().read[Time](); undeclared access fails at compile time.
API Contract ResourceStorage.add, ResourceStorage.set, ResourceStorage.remove Insert, replace or remove a value; generated entries state presence requirements and failure behavior. Resources read grants immutable access, write fresh output access, and read_write mutable access preserving existing contents. DevicePassableResource Owning resource sources opt into adapted kernel views. The selected view depends on declared access and execution target. ResourceAdapter, ResourceAccess Adapter protocol and READ, WRITE, READ_WRITE modes; fresh WRITE does not preserve prior contents. BufferResource, ReadBuffer Buffer source and immutable view for adapter-backed resources. ResourceDeviceCache Allocation cache used by the adapter protocol; it does not replace a source’s ownership or revision contract. Captures, ReadCapture, MutCapture Ordered declarations for explicitly bound host-local values, independent of resource types. read_capture, mut_capture Bind borrowed values in declaration order; keep their owners alive through the synchronous call. Ordinary resources can own heap data on sequential host execution. Device plain resources require a recursively checked pointer-free representation; an owning resource instead needs an adapter. These rules differ from the component transfer check; see compatibility.
The portable resource guide and capture guide provide independent particle programs. Reuse unchanged device copies covers revisions and escaped-reference invalidation.

Spatial classification groups entities by application-defined keys. It changes physical placement without changing an entity’s component composition or identity. Row ordering and addresses are not persistent entity identities.
API Contract SpatialClassifier Define the classification key for the registered component types. grid_cell Convert position coordinates to a grid cell using the supplied cell size. morton_key_3d Encode a three-dimensional integer cell as a Morton key within the documented coordinate limits. AtomicValue, AtomicView Own an atomic value or borrow an atomic view; operations expose their memory ordering parameters. CompareExchangeResult Reports compare-exchange success and the observed value. Synchronized, SyncView Own guarded state or borrow its view. Use nonblocking try_read or try_write and check acquisition. TryAccess Test is_acquired() before consuming the result with take(). Keep access within the acquired guard’s lifetime. The generated declarations define supported value types, origins, mutation rights and memory orderings. See maintaining particle locality and coordinating shared writes for complete examples. Synchronization does not grant undeclared component/resource access or permit structural mutation during kernel execution.

Build a particle simulation one feature at a time. Each stage is a complete program in examples/particles/.
Install Larecs: set up the locked environment and run the first program. Your first simulation: move particles with a system and a kernel, and check where they end up. Create and remove particles: create a batch of particles and remove the stationary one. Share time and configuration: set the step length from a configuration resource before each movement step. The guides cover each topic in depth: entities and components, systems and kernels, batch creation and removal, and resources.

In this tutorial you build a program that moves particles across a plane and checks where they end up. You define the particle data, write the movement logic once, and let Larecs apply it to every particle that can move.
You need a working Mojo installation and the Larecs source, as described in Installation. The tutorial assumes you can read basic Mojo: structs, functions, and var declarations.
data.check-the-result#Check the result:
After ten steps of 0.1, walker has moved one unit along x and climber two units along y. marker has not moved:
ref storage = scheduler.world.storage assert_almost_equal(storage.get[Position](walker).x, 1.0) assert_almost_equal(storage.get[Position](climber).y, 2.0) assert_almost_equal(storage.get[Position](marker).x, -3.0) print("All particles reached their expected positions.") Read components back through scheduler.world.storage with the entity handles from add_entity. assert_almost_equal tolerates the rounding error of adding 0.1 ten times.
data.create-the-world#Create the world:
A World stores all entities, components, and resources. Its parameters list every component type the world can hold:
var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(delta=0.1)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3)) add_entity creates an entity with the given components and returns its Entity handle. walker and climber have both components. marker has only a position, so move never visits it.
data.describe-particles-with-components#Descr:
An entity is a particle’s identity: a handle with no data of its own. Components are the data you attach to an entity. A particle has a position and a velocity:
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable): """Where a particle is.""" var x: Float64 """Horizontal coordinate.""" var y: Float64 """Vertical coordinate.""" @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable): """How far a particle moves per unit of time.""" var dx: Float64 """Horizontal speed.""" var dy: Float64 """Vertical speed.""" Components are ordinary structs. @fieldwise_init generates the constructor Position(x, y), and Copyable and Movable let Larecs store and move the values. Each component type appears at most once per entity.
data.next-steps#Next steps:
Continue with Create and remove particles, then Share time and configuration.
SystemContext.run lists every way to run a kernel, including the errors it raises. Inspect entities outside a kernel shows how to read entities with a query. Share values with resources covers adding, reading, and changing resources.
data.run-the-scheduler#Run the scheduler:
The Scheduler owns the world and calls your systems in the order you add them:
var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=10) world^ transfers ownership of the world to the scheduler; world is no longer usable afterwards. run(steps=10) initializes every system, calls each update ten times, and finalizes every system.
data.share-the-step-length-as-a-resource#Shar:
Every particle moves for the same amount of simulated time per step. Data that exists once for the whole simulation, rather than once per particle, is a resource:
@fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """The simulated time that passes in one step.""" var delta: Float64 """Step length."""
data.the-program#The program:
The complete program is a single file. You can open it now, or read it piece by piece below.
Complete program: examples/particles/movement.mojo """Moves particles with constant velocities for a fixed number of steps. This is the complete program of the "Your first simulation" tutorial. The `# region` and `# endregion` markers delimit the excerpts the tutorial shows. """ from std.testing import assert_almost_equal from larecs import ( Filter, KernelContext, Resources, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, World, ) @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable): """Where a particle is.""" var x: Float64 """Horizontal coordinate.""" var y: Float64 """Vertical coordinate.""" @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable): """How far a particle moves per unit of time.""" var dx: Float64 """Horizontal speed.""" var dy: Float64 """Vertical speed.""" @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """The simulated time that passes in one step.""" var delta: Float64 """Step length.""" comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Advances every particle by its velocity times the step length. Args: context: The matching rows and the declared resources. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Runs the `move` kernel once per step.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Moves all particles. Args: context: Access to the scheduler's world. Raises: Error: If `Time` is missing from the world. """ context.run[move]() def main() raises: """Runs the simulation and checks the final positions. Raises: Error: If the simulation fails or a position differs from the expected value. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(delta=0.1)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3)) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=10) ref storage = scheduler.world.storage assert_almost_equal(storage.get[Position](walker).x, 1.0) assert_almost_equal(storage.get[Position](climber).y, 2.0) assert_almost_equal(storage.get[Position](marker).x, -3.0) print("All particles reached their expected positions.")
